title: an approval swaps the rulesets' working copy whole, and the reader refuses a read that is not whole
note: basis 'shown' means shown by tests/unit/test_ruleset_swap_int_r3a.py at master 6c73db64 (the file copied in) and at the card's head, in a session container; 'read' means read in the code, not run.

findings.claim: RulesetRepo.materialize removed a ruleset's working copy, then renamed the new one in, and load_approved returned whatever it had read: with two reader processes and 200 approvals, 20 reads found no file, 15 loads were partial rulesets and 16 found no manifest; the copy is now exchanged in one rename and a read that differs from the approval tag's tree is refused as RulesetReadIncomplete (0 of each in every run)

the swap needs Linux renameat2 with RENAME_EXCHANGE; where the rulesets folder's file system has none, an approval would have written its commit and tag, then failed the swap; RulesetRepo.check_swap now probes the exchange before the approval's FHIR load, commit and tag (and before an offline install's commit and tag), and a folder that cannot swap is refused (CompileFailed step approve, from SwapUnsupported) with nothing written; there is still no fallback swap

fault type 2 outside the approval path, not fixed: materialize of a ruleset gone from its ref still removes the working copy in place (shutil.rmtree), and seed_working_copy copies the shipped rulesets into the folder in place (copytree); the tests/rulesets_guard.py docstring that described the old rmtree-then-rename is corrected

list_rulesets globbed */manifest.yaml with pathlib, which matches hidden names: while a materialisation ran, .<ruleset>.tmp was listed as a ruleset id (load_approved refused it: no approval tag); list_rulesets now skips every dot-name

omop.vocab_load.mark_rulesets reads each working copy with Ruleset.load, unchecked against the approval tag, to mark rulesets for recompilation; it uses only the manifest, which the swap now keeps whole, but a read that meets a swap can end in a FileNotFoundError, caught as OSError, and that ruleset is not marked on that load; not fixed

fail-open on a DEV or TEST box by an existing test's design: load_approved does not hold a read against an approval tag that points at nothing (tests/unit/test_new_life_1_no_preapproved_ruleset.py::test_a_broken_repository_stops_no_timer asserts such a ruleset is still listed on a TEST box); a site box refuses it in seeded_approval; left as is by the integrator's ruling

the card's own first head (514aa32): RulesetRepo.__init__ removed every .<ruleset>.tmp without a lock, and the doctor, an offline install and an update's restore open the repository too, so a second process removed a copy the compiler was building; the writer and the clean-up now hold a lock on the .git folder

a failure between an approval's tag and its swap other than an unsupported exchange (a full disk, a kill) leaves the tag and main's commit written and the whole old copy in use; nothing materialises main again at the next start, and the same version cannot be approved again (its tag exists); as before this card; not fixed

a working copy damaged on disk is refused by scenarios.approve before the compiler is called, so approving a new version of that ruleset does not repair it; an offline install or a materialisation from main does; not fixed
